graders.name: out-of-scope-has-reasons
graders.evidence:
# Team invites

Status: ux-brief

Source: briefs/team-invites-prd.md

## Problem

A workspace admin who wants to add someone has to email support, and it takes two days. Until it's done, new hires can't work. Field techs can't join the right workspace without calling the office.

## Goals and Success Metrics

- **Admins add people themselves, without support.** Signal: no support requests to add people to a workspace.
- **New hires work on day one.** Signal: 80% of invited people are working in the workspace the same day, measured by time from invite sent to first sign-in.
- **Field techs join on site from their phone.** Signal: the share of invites accepted from a phone.

## Users

- **Workspace admin**: runs a team's workspace and decides who is in it. Needs to get a new hire working on day one.
- **Field tech**: works on site from a phone, often with gloves on and poor signal. Needs to join the right workspace without calling the office.

## User Stories

1. As a workspace admin, I want to invite one person or several to my workspace by email, so that I can get a team working without waiting on support
   - Several email addresses can be entered in one go
2. As a field tech, I want to get an invite by email and join from my phone, so that I can start work on site without calling the office
   - The whole join flow works on a phone
3. As a workspace admin, I want to see the pending invites for my workspace, so that I know who hasn't joined yet
4. As a workspace admin, I want to cancel a pending invite, so that nobody joins by mistake
5. As a workspace admin, I want to resend an invite, so that someone who missed or lost it can still join
   - An expired invite can be resent, which starts a new 7 days

## Requirements

### Functional

R1. An invite expires 7 days after it is sent
R2. Resending an invite, including an expired one, starts a new 7 days
R3. The pending invites list shows each invite's state, so an admin can tell an active invite from an expired one
R4. The words "organization" and "invitation link" appear nowhere in the design: the product says "workspace" and "invite"

### Non-functional

N1. The invited person's flow is designed phone first
N2. The join flow reuses the existing sign-in screens
N3. Touch targets are large and the screens stay readable in bright light, for the field tech
N4. The join flow works with poor signal, for the field tech

## Design Scope

Yours:

- Inviting people to a workspace by email, one or several at a time
- The invited person's email and joining from a phone
- Pending invites: viewing, cancelling and resending
- Invite expiry (needs alignment, now answered: 7 days, see [question 01](team-invites/questions/01-how-long-do-invites-last.md))

Everything else the PRD covers, and who owns it, is in the [PRD snapshot](team-invites-prd.md). That includes the email template plumbing in the existing notification service, which engineering owns.

## Out of Scope

- Single sign-on: legal review of the identity provider contract isn't finished
- Inviting people to more than one workspace at once: ruled out for this release in the PRD

## Open Questions

None.
